title: Hokkien Mee (Hokkien Noodles)

items: 150g pork shoulder or pork belly (thinly sliced)
300g fresh Hokkien yellow noodles (or thick egg noodles), rinsed & drained
100g Chinese kale (or baby bok choy), cut into 2-inch lengths
Fresh chili in vinegar or prik nam som (Thai chili vinegar)

instructions.title: Step 1: Prepare sauce
steps: In a small bowl, combine:
Light soy sauce
Dark soy sauce
Oyster sauce
Sugar
Fish sauce
Stock
White pepper
Set aside.

instructions.title: Step 2: Cook protein
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add pork slices and stir-fry until nearly cooked.
Add shrimp (and squid if using) and stir-fry until just turning pink.
Remove protein from wok and set aside.

instructions.title: Step 3: Aromatics and vegetables
steps: Add a bit more oil to the same wok. Sauté garlic and onions until fragrant.
Add Chinese kale and toss for 30 seconds.
Add the noodles and toss to combine.

instructions.title: Step 4: Combine and sauce
steps: Return cooked protein to the wok.
Pour the sauce over the noodles.
Toss everything well to coat the noodles in sauce. Let it cook for 2–3 minutes, letting the sauce reduce and absorb slightly.

instructions.title: Step 5: Finish
steps: Taste and adjust seasoning: add a touch more sugar or fish sauce if needed.
Drizzle with sesame oil if using.
Toss in bean sprouts just before serving for crunch (optional).

instructions.title: To Serve
steps: Top with fried shallots.
Serve with lime wedges and chili vinegar on the side.
Best served hot, straight from the wok.

tips: Wok hei (the smoky sear) is key — use very high heat and a large wok.
Avoid overcooking shrimp; they should be just pink and firm.
Use homemade stock for deeper flavor.
